author: nflaig
content:
<@&1458826346896687229> any final thoughts on https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/pull/165, otherwise are you fine with it?

(also side note, is anyone planning to run a builder on plataberget?)

author: vladimir_ea
content: since it is decided to keep this api can you clarify what exactly you expect builders to do when they receive this request?

author: vladimir_ea
content: and is it considered manadatory for builders to implement this api?

author: vladimir_ea
content:
I guess this: 
```
A success response (202) indicates that the signed beacon block was valid. If the signed beacon block was invalid, then the builder must return an error response (400) with a description of the validation failure.
```
so is gossiping of the `SignedBeaconBlock` gated on a 202 response from the builder?

author: vladimir_ea
content: if so, what is supposed to happen on error response?

author: nflaig
content: maybe this should be clarified in the specs but the idea is that the builder can help to disseminate the block, you also have a better view as a builder to see how the block is being distributed, and most likely, builders have a better connection that validators. Not sure how builders do this today, but if you use a vanilla beacon node then you would just call `publishBlockV2`

author: nflaig
content: I would prefer it to be mandatory, currently I will log a warning on lodestar if a builder doesn't implement it, but it's non fatal since block is still gossiped via p2p

author: vladimir_ea
content: and what will you do if the builder returns an error indicating that they think the block is not valid?

author: nflaig
content: I will echo anything the builder returns as a warning

author: nflaig
content: if the local beacon node determines it's valid, it will still gossip the block itself

author: nflaig
content: the beacon node doesn't require the builder to publish the block, so even if you return an error, the proposer will still publish the beacon block via p2p

author: nflaig
content: this is obviously different from today since proposers only have the blinded beacon block which cannot be published

author: vladimir_ea
content: ok, so although the spec says 'must return an error' it actually doesn't matter what the builder returns?

author: nflaig
content: the spec defines how the api behaves, not what the caller (beacon node in this case) does with it

author: vladimir_ea
content: fair enough, however, sometimes the things specs define serve a purpose

author: nflaig
content: it should be rare that the beacon block is valid on the proposers beacon node, while the builder rejects it as invalid, but in that case, it would still be good to signal that back to the proposer, even if it's just informational
